featured_reviews.name: Uttam Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a South Indian living in Andheri East, I’m always on the lookout for places that serve authentic South Indian breakfast. While the sheer number of Udupi-style restaurants in the area are okay—or kaam chalau, as we say in Mumbai—none of them really compare to the food back home.
Neyyi is a very welcome change.
The Davangere benne dose hit the right spot—perfectly crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. The potato bhaji served alongside was creamy, well-balanced, and complemented the dosa beautifully. The podi thatte idli was soft and fluffy, with just the right amount of spice in the podi—flavourful without being overpowering, making it enjoyable for all spice tolerance levels.
The real surprise, though, was the cold filter coffee. While I initially considered the idea of cold filter coffee borderline blasphemous, it absolutely works. In fact, I’d happily take this over any cold latte or frappuccino. I’d go so far as to say I’d visit Neyyi just for their cold filter coffee alone.
I’m genuinely glad I stumbled upon this place. For people in Andheri East and Powai, this is the destination for South Indian breakfast cravings—no need to look elsewhere.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gurukripa Bar on Saki Vihar Road, Powai is one of those classic neighbourhood bars that has built a strong reputation purely on the strength of its food. I recently visited with friends and overall had a very satisfying experience, making it a solid 4-star destination for anyone in and around Powai looking for good food and a lively evening.

Let me start with the food, which is undoubtedly the highlight here. We ordered several starters along with a basic main course, and every dish was well-prepared and full of flavour. The absolute star of the meal was the mutton — incredibly tender, perfectly cooked, and rich in taste. If you are a mutton lover, this place will not disappoint you. In fact, the Dehati Mutton is a must-try. It is slow-cooked beautifully, packed with traditional flavours, and has that authentic rustic taste that is hard to find these days. Easily one of the best mutton dishes you can have in this area.

The starters were fresh and satisfying, and the gravies paired very well with rotis and rice. Portion sizes are generous, making it a good value-for-money place when dining with friends or in a group.

Another thing that truly impressed me was the speed of service. Even when the bar is packed, the staff manages to serve food in a decent amount of time. This shows excellent coordination between the kitchen and the service team, which is not easy to maintain during peak hours. Despite the crowd, our orders arrived quickly and were served hot, which added to the overall positive experience.

That said, timing your visit is extremely important. I would strongly recommend avoiding Friday nights unless you enjoy a loud, high-energy crowd. The place gets extremely crowded with corporate groups, and after 7 PM, finding a table becomes next to impossible. It also gets very noisy, which personally is not my preference when I want to relax and have a peaceful conversation with friends. I prefer quieter places, and Friday nights here can feel overwhelming.

If you still plan to visit on a busy day, the best time to reach is between 6:30 PM and 7 PM. After that, the crowd increases rapidly.

The ambience is typical of a popular local bar — lively, energetic, and social. It’s not a luxury lounge, but it has its own charm for people who enjoy a bustling atmosphere.

I am also cutting one star and giving 4 stars instead of 5 because of the pan shop owner outside the bar. I strongly believe these pan shops are indirectly part of the bar experience, and it is every bar’s responsibility to ensure that the outside environment is managed well. The first impression matters, and it should reflect the quality inside.

Overall, Gurukripa Bar delivers where it matters most — excellent food, especially mutton, fast service, and good value for money. With smart timing and the right expectations, it’s a fantastic place for a satisfying evening out.

If you go, don’t miss the Dehati Mutton — it’s an absolute must-try.
